name: Raqcoin
milestone_note: The 2018 milestone is ABCMint genesis, not UOV deployment. Community materials describe a 2022 rename.
signing: RainbowPro and UOV configurations; multisig is a separate capability.
crypto_agility: Key configuration selects the signing scheme. Existing keys do not change automatically.
limits: Since the upgrade at fork height 267120, new keys default to Rainbow configuration 274, with no public break. Keys made before the upgrade use the legacy Rainbow(16,32,32,32) parameters, publicly broken in 2022 (Kannwischer and Panny). Nodes still verify signatures from those older keys so their coins can move; coins left on them are at risk and should move to new keys. Whether the official client's prebuilt signing library does the same was not checked. NIST UOV candidate parameters are not Raqcoin deployment parameters.

name: Mochimo
milestone_note: Mainnet launched in June 2018.
signing: WOTS+ transaction signatures.
crypto_agility: One active signing scheme in the reviewed material.
limits: The switch to proof of stake rests on the project's website alone; the public node repository still shows PoW code. The signing scheme remained WOTS+. No claim that a future protocol upgrade could never change it.

name: QRL
milestone_note: Mainnet launched in June 2018.
signing: XMSS transaction signatures.
crypto_agility: Hash-function choice and descriptor fields; not arbitrary switching between signature families.
limits: XMSS is stateful. The RFC size example is not QRL transaction serialization.

name: Nexus
milestone_note: November 2019 is the Tritium upgrade, not the original chain genesis in 2014.
signing: Opt-in Falcon-512; classical Brainpool signatures remain valid.
crypto_agility: Signature chains commit to a subsequent key and scheme.
limits: Do not treat every Nexus account as post-quantum.

name: Tidecoin
milestone_note: Genesis was December 27, 2020.
signing: Falcon-512 active; Falcon-1024 and ML-DSA exist in upgrade code.
crypto_agility: Multiple schemes are implemented behind an activation gate.
limits: Implemented upgrade support does not establish that it is active on mainnet.

name: Starknet
milestone_note: November 2021 is L2 Mainnet Alpha, not an independent L1 launch.
signing: STARK validity proofs. Falcon-512 account classes are declared on mainnet (an OpenZeppelin pre-release and S2morrow); none has a published audit.
crypto_agility: Account abstraction and contract upgrades can change account verification logic.
limits: The Falcon-512 account classes are pre-release or experimental and have no published audit, and existing accounts must move to them one by one. Ethereum settlement and bridge dependencies remain. The L1 vote supported research, not a move.

name: Abelian
milestone_note: Mainnet launched in April 2022.
signing: Custom lattice-based PQRingCT/PQRingCTX schemes.
crypto_agility: Versioned cryptographic schemes; mining algorithm choice is a separate matter.
limits: These schemes are not ML-DSA. Dual PoW does not mean PoW plus PoS. QDay is a separate L2.

name: Algorand
milestone_note: The timeline uses the 2022 State Proofs milestone. The chain launched in 2019.
signing: Falcon State Proofs and opt-in Falcon account authorization.
crypto_agility: Rekeying and programmable authorization; native Falcon-1024 accounts are also documented.
limits: State Proofs and account signing have different roles. Consensus participation keys remain classical; app and wallet support still matters.

name: Cellframe
milestone_note: Native mainnet launched in July 2023.
signing: Native-wallet options include Dilithium, Falcon and SPHINCS+.
crypto_agility: Multiple native signing schemes, subject to network and wallet support.
limits: Scope is native CF-20 assets, not ERC-20/BEP-20 tokens. Picnic is a historical/deprecated route, not a current wallet option in this release.

name: QuantumCoin
milestone_note: Mainnet launched on December 31, 2023.
signing: Hybrid post-quantum and Ed25519 signing; ML-DSA and SLH-DSA components.
crypto_agility: Signing modes change at protocol thresholds and in emergency mode.
limits: Do not assume every protocol phase uses exactly the same component combination. ML-KEM node handshakes are not transaction signatures.

name: QANplatform
milestone_note: May 2024 is the public testnet announcement, not a public mainnet launch.
signing: XLINK pairs ML-DSA-65 with secp256k1.
crypto_agility: A fixed signature pairing in the reviewed XLINK path.
limits: The traded QANX token does not establish a live native post-quantum mainnet. The original 2024 announcement used the Dilithium name; do not backdate current parameters.

name: Neptune Cash
milestone_note: First launch in February 2025; the current chain relaunched on August 5, 2025.
signing: Hash-preimage spending conditions and Triton STARK validity proofs.
crypto_agility: Programmable lock scripts.
limits: A STARK proof and a hash-preimage spending condition are not a fixed-size standard digital signature.

name: Nervos CKB
timeline_milestone: Jan · SPHINCS+ lock deployed on mainnet
milestone_note: January 2026 marks the SPHINCS+ lock deployment. CKB mainnet launched in 2019.
signing: An opt-in SPHINCS+ spending lock.
crypto_agility: New verification logic can be deployed as lock scripts.
limits: Existing cells must satisfy their old spending rules before migration. Default secp256k1 cells do not change automatically.

name: Quantus
milestone_note: Mainnet launched on September 9, 2026.
signing: ML-DSA-87 and ML-DSA-65 transaction signing.
crypto_agility: Parameter-set selection within ML-DSA.
limits: ML-DSA-65 requires runtime spec 139 or later and compatible account tooling. Quantus and qtcchain both use QTC but are separate chains.

name: xCoin
milestone_note: The project whitepaper dates mainnet genesis to September 26, 2026.
signing: ML-DSA-65 primary signing; SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s fallback leaves.
crypto_agility: Cross-family fallback requires committing to the alternative spending leaf in advance.
limits: This is not a claim that every spend carries both signatures or that a new fallback can be added after a key is compromised.

name: qtcchain
milestone_note: v1 launched September 30, 2026; v2 re-genesis was October 5, 2026.
signing: ML-DSA-44 primary signing; SLH-DSA fallback/multisig.
crypto_agility: Per-key scheme selection and multiple script leaves.
limits: Falcon is reserved in the reviewed specification. qtcchain is unrelated to Quantus despite the shared QTC ticker. The repository records a v2 treasury allocation; inclusion is not a fair-launch endorsement.

name: Soqucoin
milestone_note: Mainnet block 1 was mined on October 13, 2026.
signing: ML-DSA-44 transaction signing.
crypto_agility: One active transaction-signing scheme in the snapshot.
limits: XMSS experiments are not counted as a mainnet signing path. Public blocks do not establish user adoption or independent security certification.

name: Splendor Quantum
milestone_note: The current mainnet genesis was minted on September 21, 2026, after earlier resets.
signing: ML-DSA-65 for native transactions, blocks and validator votes; addresses are SHA3-256 of the public key.
crypto_agility: One account signing scheme; the SQVL module adds dual ML-DSA-65 + SLH-DSA instructions.
limits: SPLD on the legacy Splendor EVM chain 2691 is a separate network until migrated. The repository states there is no third-party audit.

name: Qbit
milestone_note: Mainnet genesis was July 15, 2026; Qbit Core v1.0.0 followed on July 16.
signing: OP_CHECKSIGPQC with a single SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s-bounded30 profile inside P2MR outputs.
crypto_agility: One active profile; reserved leaf versions allow a later soft fork to add another.
limits: The bounded profile is not a FIPS 205 parameter set and is safe only up to 2^30 signatures per key.

name: Discrete
milestone_note: The project dates mainnet to July 15, 2026.
signing: ML-DSA-65 spend authorization; ML-KEM-768 encapsulation for output delivery.
crypto_agility: One active signing scheme; changing frozen parameters requires a hard fork.
limits: Spending reveals the long-term spend key and amounts are public in Phase 1; finality is node-local.

name: Dilithion
milestone_note: The repository dates the mainnet launch (a fair-launch reset) to January 28, 2026.
signing: Dilithium mode 3 from the FIPS 204 reference code, i.e. ML-DSA-65 sizes and encoding.
crypto_agility: One active signing scheme.
limits: DIL bridged to Base relies on Base accounts, not on Dilithium. The project uses the Dilithium3 name rather than ML-DSA-65.

name: Parano1d
milestone_note: Mainnet genesis was August 21, 2026; v2 releases followed in October 2026.
signing: No public-key transaction signature: spends prove knowledge of a secret's Poseidon2b preimage.
crypto_agility: Protocol versions activate at announced heights.
limits: A zero-knowledge proof of a hash preimage is not a standard digital signature, and the proof stack is not standardized. P2P peer identity uses Ed25519.

name: Aere Network
milestone_note: Type-0x50 ML-DSA transactions were enabled on chain 2800 from block 19,900,000 (September 23, 2026).
signing: Opt-in ML-DSA-44/65/87 transactions beside the default secp256k1 path; Falcon-512 and SLH-DSA validator seals.
crypto_agility: The ML-DSA parameter set is chosen per transaction by an algorithm identifier.
limits: PQ accounts are opt-in; secp256k1 accounts, node transport and part of each consensus message remain classical. No completed third-party audit.

name: QoreChain
milestone_note: Mainnet block 1 is dated June 29, 2026.
signing: Every Cosmos-lane transaction carries a classical and an ML-DSA-87 signature; mainnet parameters require the hybrid form.
crypto_agility: Enforcement mode (disabled/optional/required) and key migration are governed on chain.
limits: EVM transactions inside an open window are authorized by secp256k1 alone, and validator keys are classical.

name: Minima
milestone_note: CoinMarketCap dates the native coin's launch to November 26, 2024; no project source dating the mainnet launch was found.
signing: KISS VM signature checks verify TreeKey signatures built from Winternitz one-time signatures (SHA3-256, w = 8).
crypto_agility: Coins are locked by scripts, so the locking logic is programmable; the signature primitive itself is fixed in the node.
limits: One-time keys depend on correct use tracking, and the Winternitz key-tree construction is not a standardized scheme.
